description: Defence Industry Security Programme Entry Level requirements for Australian defence supply chain participation

domains.description: Organisational security management, policies, and oversight
Workforce security screening, awareness, and management
Information protection and cyber defence controls

requirements.requirement_text: The organisation must have a documented security policy that is approved by senior management and communicated to all personnel.
The organisation must appoint a Security Officer responsible for implementing and maintaining the security program.
The organisation must conduct regular security risk assessments to identify threats and vulnerabilities to defence-related information and assets.
The organisation must maintain a security incidents register and have procedures for reporting security incidents to Defence.
The organisation must have documented procedures for managing security clearances and ensure only cleared personnel access classified information.
The organisation must conduct annual security awareness training for all personnel with access to defence information.
The organisation must have a documented business continuity plan that addresses protection of defence information during disruptions.
The organisation must maintain an inventory of all defence-related information and assets, including their security classification.
The organisation must have procedures for secure destruction of classified and sensitive defence information.
The organisation must conduct due diligence on subcontractors and suppliers who will have access to defence information.
The organisation must have contractual arrangements with subcontractors that include security obligations equivalent to DISP requirements.
The organisation must conduct periodic security audits and reviews of its security program effectiveness.
The organisation must have documented procedures for handling, storing, and transmitting classified information.
The organisation must maintain records of security briefings and debriefings for personnel with access to defence information.
The organisation must verify the identity and right to work of all personnel before granting access to defence information or facilities.
The organisation must conduct pre-employment screening including criminal history checks for personnel who will access defence information.
The organisation must ensure personnel hold appropriate security clearances before granting access to classified information.
The organisation must conduct security induction briefings for all new personnel with access to defence information.
The organisation must have procedures for reporting changes in personnel circumstances that may affect their security status.
The organisation must conduct security debriefings when personnel with access to defence information leave the organisation.
The organisation must maintain records of all personnel security clearances, briefings, and access authorisations.
The organisation must implement physical access controls to prevent unauthorised access to areas where defence information is stored or processed.
The organisation must use appropriate security containers or facilities for storing classified defence information when not in use.
The organisation must maintain visitor management procedures including identification verification, escorts, and access logs.
The organisation must implement access controls to ensure only authorised personnel can access defence information on IT systems.
The organisation must use encryption for electronic storage and transmission of classified or sensitive defence information.
The organisation must implement measures to protect IT systems from malware, including antivirus software and regular updates.
The organisation must maintain audit logs of access to defence information on IT systems and review them regularly.
